sanskrit_verse:
पूर्णे प्रकर्षे तत्साम्यम् उभयोः परिकीर्तितम् ।
अपूर्णे तु प्रकुर्यातां प्रस्परमतेन तौ ॥७१॥
transliteration: pūrṇe prakarṣe tatsāmyam ubhayoḥ parikīrtitam / apūrṇe tu prakuryātāṃ prasparamatena tau
sph_interpretive_translation: When both parties are whole and equal in capacity, their equivalence is declared; when incomplete, they shall act according to mutual consent.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from completeness of being
Causation flows from conscious capacity, not external force
Restoration occurs through alignment of mutual recognition
executable_legal_axioms: IF (party_A.capacity == complete AND party_B.capacity == complete) THEN equivalence_must_be_declared
IF (party_A.capacity == incomplete OR party_B.capacity == incomplete) THEN actions_must_follow_mutual_consent_protocol
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that where litigants possess full existential and operational capacity, equality before dharma must be recognized without exception. Where incompleteness is evident, resolution proceeds only upon verified mutual assent. The threshold of responsibility is determined by the degree of conscious completion, not social status or legal fiction.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that true causality lies in the completeness of participants’ consciousness. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that incomplete states manifest sequentially due to lack of self-assumption. Proportional responsibility aligns with capacity awareness. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that imbalance resolves through mutual restoration rather than imposed judgment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Completion Process for all parties with identified gaps in self-awareness
Establish Mutual Consent Verification Protocol prior to proceeding with any legal determination
Deploy Consciousness Reintegration Module to restore wholeness in incomplete entities
Apply Integrity Alignment Sequence to ensure congruence between intent, action, and recognition
Execute Restorative Witnessing Framework wherein both parties acknowledge each other's completeness
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Dharma. This law restores balance through conscious equivalence. Justice operates solely for reintegration and alignment. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator.
